publicReleaseNotes: A Recover test event now closes the alert it follows. On an Events API source, Send a test event remembers the last accepted Trigger and fills in its alert key and generation, so a Recover sent after you visit Alerts or reload closes that same alert, whatever its severity; a declared incident stays open. A new Events API source now shows its endpoint and a ready-to-send request as soon as it is created, and a source that has received nothing yet keeps that request open, so the next step is visible. Acknowledging an incident now keeps the lead you chose: Acknowledge makes you the assignee and leaves the chosen lead in place, and if no lead was set you become lead as well. The people pickers and the incident guide say this in plain words. The README now shows the one required PATH step after the installer: a terminal without ~/.local/bin on PATH needs export PATH="$HOME/.local/bin:$PATH" first, or it says rer: command not found. The pinned rer is now 0.2.108, which refreshes the copied Base runtime; this update adds no migration. Back up first as in earlier updates, keep applied migrations unchanged, and keep the existing pager active: paging stays OFF.

agentUpdateInstructions: From 0.5.1, back up local data with rer export --output exports/before-0.5.8.rer. For a hosted installation, export its D1 database with npx wrangler d1 export DATABASE --remote --output exports/DATABASE.sql using the original deploying Cloudflare credentials; DATABASE is recorded in .rer/deploy/ENVIRONMENT.json. Keep the backup private. Stop the local app with Ctrl-C, run git pull --ff-only, then rer dev; from a detached release tag use git fetch --tags && git checkout v0.5.8 instead of git pull --ff-only. For a hosted installation, update the original deploying checkout and run rer deploy --environment ENVIRONMENT with the same credentials. The update adds 18 migrations (0146-0163); retain all 67 migration files unchanged and do not reset a populated installation. The checkout pins rer 0.2.108 and installs it through the pinned tooling. Restore only into an empty destination with rer import --input exports/before-0.5.8.rer --yes, then check the owner, schedules, incidents and agent settings. Paging stays OFF; keep the existing pager active. Earlier upgrade instructions follow. From 0.4.2 or from the unreleased v0.5.0 tag, back up local data with rer export --output exports/before-0.5.1.rer. For a hosted installation, export its D1 database with npx wrangler d1 export DATABASE --remote --output exports/DATABASE.sql using the deploying CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID and CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN; DATABASE is recorded in .rer/deploy/ENVIRONMENT.json. Keep the backup private. Stop the local app with Ctrl-C, run git pull --ff-only, then rer dev; from a checkout of the v0.5.0 tag run git fetch --tags && git checkout v0.5.1 instead of git pull --ff-only. To update from 0.3.0, back up first: locally with `rer export --output exports/NAME.rer`; for a hosted installation export its D1 database with `npx wrangler d1 export DATABASE --remote --output exports/DATABASE.sql` (the name is in `.rer/deploy/ENVIRONMENT.json`) using the deploying Cloudflare credentials. Locally, stop `rer dev` with Ctrl-C, run `git pull --ff-only`, then `rer dev`. Hosted, from the checkout that deployed, run `git pull --ff-only` and `rer deploy --environment ENVIRONMENT` with the same credentials; the owner, schedules and incidents are kept. The update applies ten additive migrations (0117-0126); keep all 32 applied migrations unchanged and do not reset to upgrade. Restore a backup only into an empty destination (`rer import --input exports/NAME.rer --yes` locally, a fresh empty installation when hosted). Paging stays OFF; keep your existing pager active. From 0.2.0, stop with `rer dev --stop` and `rer preview --stop`, then run `git pull --ff-only` and `rer dev`. The update applies four additive migrations (0113–0116); keep all 22 applied migrations unchanged and do not reset to upgrade. Data, the owner and password accounts are kept. People who sign in with a workspace password sign in once more, because the held session cookie is now named `oncall_session_<port>`. Captured local sign-in mail is removed with the development outbox; open the app with the `RER_OPEN` link that `rer dev` prints. To update from 0.1.0, stop the old servers before pulling with `node scripts/rer.mjs dev --stop` and `node scripts/rer.mjs preview --stop`, install the global rer command with `curl -fsSL https://runeditrun.com/install.sh | sh` (or `npm install -g @runeditrun/rer`), then run `git pull --ff-only` and `rer dev`. Back up first with `rer export --output exports/NAME.rer` (0.1.0: `node scripts/rer.mjs export --output exports/NAME.rer` while its servers are stopped). Restore only into an empty destination with `rer import --input exports/NAME.rer --yes` after restoring the original private settings. For hosted coordination, follow Install and run → Host for your team: configure remote sign-in mail and run `rer deploy` with your Cloudflare credentials; rer claims the owner and retires the setup token. Open the app address and sign in by emailed link, or with `rer signin`. Update an existing hosted installation with `rer deploy`, preserving its owner and data. Remove with `rer deploy --remove --yes` and confirm its empty readback. Paging stays OFF; keep your existing pager active. Independent standby and paging delivery are outside this release.
